timeline_events.description: Baseline connection pool utilization is healthy at 2 of 20 active connections.
Connection pool hits full saturation (20/20 active connections).
Gateway begins returning HTTP 504 timeouts to citizens due to auth-service upstream delay.

evidence.note: First observed 504 status code span on gateway

timeline_events.description: Auth-service fails to acquire database connection before timeout due to connection leak on unhandled error paths.

evidence.note: Log line confirming pool exhausted (20/20 active) at corrected timestamp
Log line confirming unhandled exception skipped release()

timeline_events.description: Frontend CPU spikes to 88.5% due to aggressive client retry storm following gateway 504s.

evidence.note: CPU onset lagged gateway 504 onset by 30 seconds
Client log indicating exponential backoff retry storm initiated

hypotheses_evaluated.statement: auth-service leaks DB connections on error path, exhausting db-pool and causing gateway 504 timeouts.

supporting.note: Active connections reached pool max 20 before any 504s occurred
Explicit leak detected in auth-service token validator

model_assumptions: Discrete event queue model of connection pool

hypotheses_evaluated.statement: Frontend CPU exhaustion caused slow request processing and subsequent gateway timeouts.

supporting.note: High CPU utilization observed during incident

refuting.note: Gateway errors began 30 seconds before frontend CPU elevated

model_assumptions: Eliminating frontend retries does not restore leaked db connections

remediation: Wrap db connection acquisition in try-finally or context manager to guarantee release() on all exit paths.
Introduce circuit breaker at gateway to shed load when auth-service latency degrades.
